page: Microsoft Azure F2-1amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor core operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high 1:16 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is bundled with a 236 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to its single-core configuration, the server achieves top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and database operations fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is average for large block operations but weak for cached small blocks. Static web serving throughput is poor, and LLM inference is limited, with text generation on a medium 7B model reaching only 5.3 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2-1amds_v7 offers a specialized resource profile, providing a high density of memory and local storage relative to its single compute core. This makes it a highly targeted option for workloads that require significant memory capacity and fast single-threaded execution but do not benefit from multi-threaded parallelism. Suitable workloads include memory-heavy single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, and basic database tasks with low concurrent query volumes.
